newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem's image bounces back after hitting bottom.
newsitem.headline: Menem's image bounces back after hitting bottom.

text.p: President Carlos Menem's image recovered slightly this month, with nearly one out of five Argentines saying they think he is doing a good job, an opinion poll showed Sunday.

Eighteen percent of respondents told the poll conducted by the private group Centro de Estudios para la Nueva Mayoria and published by the daily La Nacion that they had a good opinion of the president's performance, up from a dismal 14 percent at the previous quarterly measurement.

La Nacion pointed out that the poll of 1,030 people conducted in the first week of March showed support of Menem picked up, however timidly, at a time when a scandal over the source of funds for the construction of a major runway in his minuscule hometown was making headline news throughout the country.

Menem won a second term in office with half the votes in 1995, but his public support has taken a nosedive since. It hit rock bottom in the last quarterly measurement at the end of last year, when only 14 percent of the people said they approved of his job.

People's opinion of his economic policies have fared even worse, trailing the presidential image's downward path a few points behind. In keeping with the trend, it bounced back in the first quarter 1997 to 15 percent from an all-time low of 11 percent in the last three months of 1996.

His free-market economic policies, which returned the country to a path of growth and currency stability after years of hyperinflation, devaluations and stagnation, were in the past the most solid pillar of popular support for his government.

But a 17.3 percent unemployment rate which has displayed a strong resistance to official cures has undermined people's adherence to tough austerity policies which have meant layoffs of public workers, higher taxes and wage cuts.

People's backing both for Menem and his economic policies is greater among the less educated, with 28 percent of those with only grammar school education expressing a good opinion of the president, against only five percent among university graduates.
The poll conducted in Buenos Aires and its outskirts has a margin of error of 4.5 percent.
